title: Buffett's 2023 letter: wonderful businesses, permanent-loss avoidance, and fortress balance sheets
summary: Buffett's 2023 shareholder letter, written after Munger's death, covers why Berkshire reports operating rather than GAAP earnings, why it buys wonderful businesses at fair prices, and why it never risks permanent loss of capital. It also covers the capital-intensity of BNSF, his utility mistake, insurance underwriting discipline, and why he trusts patient owners like his sister Bertie.

principles.text: Buy wonderful businesses at fair prices, not fair businesses at wonderful prices; Graham-style cheapness only works at small scale.
principles.quote: add to it wonderful businesses purchased at fair prices and give up buying fair businesses at wonderful prices. In other words, abandon everything you learned from your hero, Ben Graham. It works but only when practiced at small scale.”

principles.text: Never risk permanent loss of capital; a few good decisions plus avoiding serious mistakes is enough over a lifetime.
principles.quote: One investment rule at Berkshire has not and will not change: Never risk permanent loss of capital.

principles.text: Favor rare businesses that can deploy more capital at high returns; owning one and sitting tight can create enormous wealth.
principles.quote: At Berkshire, we particularly favor the rare enterprise that can deploy additional capital at high returns in the future. Owning only one of these companies – and simply sitting tight – can deliver wealth almost beyond measure.

principles.text: Repurchases only make sense at a discount to business value; at a premium they are stupid.
principles.quote: All stock repurchases should be price-dependent. What is sensible at a discount to business-value becomes stupid if done at a premium.

principles.text: You cannot reliably judge managers by sincerity; never deal with a rascal expecting to prevent cheating.
principles.quote: “Never deal with a rascal under the expectation that you can prevent him from cheating you.” Many bankers who thought they could “manage” the rascal problem have learned the wisdom of Mr. McCulloch’s advice – and I have as well.

principles.text: Insurance underwriters cannot be optimists, since P/C surprises are almost always negative.
principles.quote: our underwriters can be thin, fat, male, female, young, old, foreign or domestic. But they can’t be optimists at the office, however desirable that quality may generally be in life.
